# ISSUE-57 implementation plan

Make isolated agent deadlines policy-driven and retain recoverable work without importing failed runs.

**Shape: Involved.** This crosses config validation, trusted policy propagation, four interactive harness loops, OCI lifecycle, safe filesystem export, and checkpoint exclusion. Keep it one WorkUnit because these pieces jointly establish the timeout safety contract; require the configured independent agent plan gate before implementation. No protected harness changes are needed.

## What we know

- `internal/agent/isolated.go:41` supplies a 15-minute timeout; `internal/sandbox/native.go:315` and `internal/sandbox/worker.go:347` independently cap execution at 15 minutes. Both workspace paths return on execution failure before importing results and defer snapshot/container cleanup.
- `internal/contract/execution.go:17` defines execution policy; `internal/harness/scaffold.go:563` (`decodeConfig`) already invokes `ResolveExecution`, so central duration validation can reach doctor and validate without changing repository policy files.
- Execution uses approved configuration (`internal/workflow/engine.go:247,434`, `internal/cli/claim_helpers.go:38`); `NewConfiguredRunner` currently retains boundary settings but no timeout policy (`internal/agent/configured.go`). Never reload config inside a worker.
- Coordinator-owned input waits exist in `RunNativeCodex`, `RunDelegatedHarness`, `runOpenCode`, and `runOMP` (`internal/sandbox/native.go:287`, `delegated.go:171`, `opencode.go:131`, `omp.go:217`). OMP waits until session settlement before asking for input; tool activity is not operator idle time.
- Native validation also uses `withNativeWorkspace`; OCI validation supplies its check duration with `DiscardChanges` (`internal/validation/validator.go:150`). Agent budget changes must not change validation-check timeout semantics.
- Recovery needs explicit publication exclusion: `Checkpoint` uses `git add -A` (`internal/workspace/worktree.go:375`), and snapshot packing excludes several coordinator directories but not all active-output files (`internal/sandbox/worker.go:638`).
- `safeRunFailure` deliberately masks error strings (`internal/agent/failure.go:19`); a recovery error must expose only coordinator-generated metadata through that wrapper.
- `internal/safefs/root.go` provides pinned roots, safe directory creation, regular-file checks, and atomic replacement. Existing snapshot pack/unpack rejects unsafe entries. OCI read-only outputs live in `/output`, with coordinator-installed links in `/workspace` (`internal/sandbox/worker.go:405`).

## Decided timeout semantics

The prior review accepted these semantics: role overrides beat the global setting; unattended runs default to 60m. Native Codex and harness-tools interactive runs default to a cumulative 60m active budget with an independent 4h wall cap. Explicit policy sets the cumulative active budget to min(configured value, 4h), with an independent fixed 4h wall cap. Clamp values above 4h in the resolver for every interactive backend; unattended configured values are not subject to this interactive clamp. Interactive OCI defaults to 4h wall time; explicit global/role policy shortens that to min(configured value, 4h), with no idle exclusion. Values above 4h cannot extend interactive execution. Keep resolver tests, doctor and docs consistent.

## Decided recovery bound

Use an 8 MiB total recovery patch bound, with per-file and entry limits selected against existing worker budgets in step 1. Omit whole oversized or binary entries with explicit coordinator-generated notices; never cut hunks to fit the bound.

## What we're assuming
- Existing fake-runtime fixtures can exercise timeout export lifecycle without a qualification image; check this first in step 1.

## Open questions

- Can each supported OCI runtime pause/export after deadline cancellation without losing tmpfs? Step 1 uses existing fake-runtime fixtures to establish the recovery sequence; optional local runtime checks confirm it. No new image or turn protocol.
- Which checkpoint/submission paths can include an already tracked or staged recovery file? Step 1 traces them and step 6 adds an explicit rejection/exclusion regression; an ignore rule alone is insufficient.

## Design and alternatives

Use a single pure resolver in `internal/contract` and a shared coordinator-owned budget controller in `internal/sandbox`. Retain the resolved policy on the configured adapter. A single wall-clock context cannot exclude operator think-time; resetting a timeout each turn incorrectly grants unlimited aggregate working time. Instead track cumulative active time across turns and a separate fixed four-hour interactive wall deadline. Pause active accounting only immediately around coordinator-owned input reads, never based on output silence or model-supplied timestamps. Parent cancellation always wins.

Capture recovery from a validated immutable baseline and stopped/frozen sandbox, never from the live checkout or by applying changes. Use the same recovery writer for native, delegated, and OCI backends, including read-only role output mapping. `internal/agent/isolated.go:44` assigns reviewer `OutputDir` under the request worktree; `internal/agent/review.go:RunReview` redirects the request into its isolated review snapshot before execution. Trace both layers so timeout recovery reaches the intended live diagnostic directory without importing partial `REVIEW.md`. Recovery is diagnostic local output, never a successful role artifact. Keep validation execution separate from agent budgets; do not add timeout flags unless a real existing override path requires plumbing. Any operator override must be positive and may only reduce policy.

## Files, symbols, and sequence

1. Inspect existing worker manifests/budgets, snapshot import rules, OCI stop/pause/export behavior, `RunNativeValidation`, and all checkpoint/submission paths. Add small deterministic lifecycle fixtures to settle the open questions before changing execution. If safe OCI export cannot be established with current runtime primitives, stop for plan revision rather than silently reducing acceptance.
2. Extend `ExecutionConfig` in `internal/contract/execution.go` with presence-aware `AgentTimeout` and per-role `RoleTimeouts` duration strings (YAML/JSON names from the contract). Add `ResolveAgentTimeout` and resolved budget type in new `internal/contract/timeout.go`. Parse Go durations; distinguish omitted from explicitly empty values, reject non-positive/overflow/malformed durations and unknown role keys; validate every override even for unselected roles. Call validation from `ResolveExecution`. Default unattended active budget to 60m; interactive wall cap is 4h; native interactive active budget defaults to 60m, OCI interactive has no idle exclusion. Role overrides take precedence over the global value. For interactive native/delegated runs clamp the configured cumulative active budget to 4h; for interactive OCI resolve the wall limit to min(configured value, 4h), defaulting to 4h. Keep the independent native/delegated wall cap fixed at 4h. Resolve warning lead as min(2m, 10% of the applicable budget). No new config keys beyond those requested.
3. In `internal/agent/configured.go`, `adapters.go` (`CLIAdapter`), and `isolated.go` (`runIsolated`), retain approved execution policy and pass a resolved budget, role, interactive mode, and coordinator warning sink via `WorkerOptions`. Audit runner construction in workflow/project planning and CLI paths to preserve approved-base loading; add regression fixtures in `internal/agent/isolation_policy_test.go` and `internal/workflow/engine_test.go` (or a focused new timeout-policy test file). Candidate config never supplies execution authority.
4. Add `internal/sandbox/timeout.go` with an injectable clock/timer, cumulative active accounting, immutable wall cap, cancellation cause, and synchronized once-only warning for the first impending effective deadline. Stop timers/goroutines on every exit; do not let resume race with cancellation. Integrate `withNativeWorkspace` and `RunWorker`; remove hardcoded agent caps. In `native.go`, `delegated.go`, `opencode.go`, and `omp.go`, pause only while `nativeInstruction` awaits input and resume before dispatch. Keep setup, tool execution, and session settlement charged. Warnings name validated role and remaining duration and reach stderr/interactive terminal even while input is blocked. Keep `internal/validation/validator.go:133-139` unchanged: every required check retains min(15m, check.timeout), including a configured 20m check. `RunNativeValidation`, `RunConfiguredNativeValidation`, and validation `RunWorker` calls use only validation/caller contexts and existing check limits, with no agent budgets, warnings, or patch recovery. Add a table-driven regression test with host, native and OCI subtests: a required check configured at `20m` receives a `15m` effective deadline on every path (or an earlier caller deadline). Exercise the actual validation dispatch and sandbox entry points after removing their agent caps; validation must never pick up the agent budget, warnings or patch recovery.

   In `internal/sandbox/mcp.go:ServeTools`, replace its independent 15m timer with cancellable parent lifetime (retain cancellation/EOF cleanup). Audit `internal/cli/internal_tools.go:newInternalToolsCmd` and `delegated.go` tool-process launch: coordinator termination must close transports and stop descendants. Do not add an agent-controlled timeout flag. A delegated tool server must remain usable after 15m under longer policy, and exit at coordinator cancellation/deadline. See the deadline inventory below.
5. Add `internal/sandbox/timeout_patch.go`: compare initial snapshot bytes with final validated regular files, produce deterministic relative-path unified diffs for additions/modifications/deletions and role output files, bound input reads, diff computation, entries, output bytes, and recovery elapsed time. Include useful handling of no-final-newline, binary, and oversized files. Reject traversal, symlinks, hardlinks, FIFOs/devices/sockets and unsafe destination components; do not follow candidate paths. Write only `.swarm/active-output/<validated-role>-timeout.patch` via `safefs.Root.Sub`/`WriteFile`, mode 0600. On deadline, terminate/quiesce native processes and tools before capture; pause OCI before bounded export, read `/output` for read-only roles, then remove the container. Recovery uses a separate short coordinator context because the run context has expired, and never calls `importWorker` or role-output replacement. Preserve timeout classification if capture fails and report capture failure honestly; never claim a patch exists until atomic write succeeds.
6. Add a typed timeout error containing only trusted role, configured and effective limit/deadline kind, and fixed relative patch path. Update `internal/agent/failure.go` to render this metadata while continuing to mask arbitrary harness diagnostics and preserve `errors.Is(context.DeadlineExceeded)`. Exclude timeout patches from sandbox inputs/outputs in `worker.go`; update `internal/workspace/worktree.go` (`Checkpoint` and local excludes) and the actual submission guards found in step 1 to keep recovery files out even if staged/tracked. Audit `internal/pr/service.go:Submit`, `internal/workspace/worktree.go:PushForkCheckpoint`, and issue submission entry points; add a guard before publication where needed; never mutate checkpoint/state/artifacts on timeout. Explicitly test `internal/agent/review.go:RunReview`: do not replace live REVIEW.md with partial output and never collect reviewer-timeout.patch as a review artifact.
7. In `internal/cli/doctor.go`, add deterministic per-role resolved timeout reporting, including interactive active/wall semantics. Doctor describes the local repository config; actual runs continue to use the approved base. Verify errors flow through `internal/harness/scaffold.go:decodeConfig` and `internal/validation/validator.go` before checks execute. Extend existing CLI/harness tests.
8. Update `docs/project.md` config reference, `docs/developer.md` interrupted-run recovery, `docs/harness/README.md`, `codex.md`, `claude.md`, `opencode.md`, `omp.md`, and `CHANGELOG.md`. Explain global/per-role precedence, budgets, warning lead, OCI wall-only accounting, patch limits, and manual inspection/recovery. Keep existing per-tool deadlines distinct and unchanged. Do not change `.swarm/config.yaml`, protected schemas/prompts/workflows, validation checks, or CI.
9. Run TEST_PLAN checks and inspect the final diff for unplanned policy or publication changes. All security regression cases must fail against old behavior; retain existing adversarial coverage.

## Review requirements and implementation checkpoints

| Review finding | Required change | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Delegated MCP lifetime | Step 4 changes `ServeTools` in `internal/sandbox/mcp.go` and audits `newInternalToolsCmd` in `internal/cli/internal_tools.go` plus the coordinator launch in `delegated.go`. Use parent cancellation rather than an independent server deadline; no transport-supplied timeout authority. | TEST_PLAN R1: send a real tool request after 15 simulated minutes, then verify cancellation/deadline cleanup. |
| 2. Validation ceiling | Step 4 preserves `validator.go:133-139` and separates validation calls from agent budgets, warnings and recovery. | TEST_PLAN R2: a configured 20m check gets a 15m effective deadline on host, native and OCI. |
| 3–5. Citations, semantics and recovery bounds | Corrected native citations above; interactive budgets are decided policy; omit whole binary/oversized entries with notices. | Resolver tables and bounded patch tests in acceptance rows 2 and 6. |
| 6. Reviewer output | Step 6 prevents timeout import and review-artifact collection of recovery patches. | TEST_PLAN R3: preserve live REVIEW.md and authoritative artifacts. |

## Deadline inventory and review resolution

Re-ran the inventory during this revision and confirmed eight production deadline sites (nine matching lines), plus seven test-only occurrences. Inspection command: `grep -Rn 'time.Minute' internal --include='*.go'` (ripgrep is unavailable in this planning environment). Repeat after implementation and classify new deadlines too.

| Location | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| `internal/agent/isolated.go:41` | Replace hardcoded 15m with approved shared resolver. |
| `internal/sandbox/native.go:315` | Replace agent cap with shared controller; preserve validation caller deadlines. |
| `internal/sandbox/worker.go:347-348` | Replace agent cap with shared controller; preserve validation check deadline. |
| `internal/sandbox/mcp.go:16` | Remove independent 15m server cap; retain parent cancellation, transport cleanup and coordinator descendant termination. |
| `internal/validation/validator.go:133` | Keep 15m maximum required-check timeout unchanged. |
| `internal/sandbox/executor.go:96` | Keep 2m per-tool execution limit; this is distinct from run lifetime. |
| `internal/agent/review.go:25` | Keep 2m bounded snapshot duration; this is filesystem safety work. |
| `internal/gitcredential/token.go:23` | Keep 2m credential-command limit; coordinator only. |
| `internal/sandbox/harness_integration_test.go:62` | Keep 3m outer bound for the opt-in authenticated harness boundary test; prevents a hung integration fixture. |
| `internal/sandbox/worker_oci_test.go:25` | Keep 2m explicit fixture budget for OCI integration tests; resolve it through coordinator policy plumbing as needed, without making it the production default. |
| `internal/sandbox/worker_oci_test.go:173` | Keep 1m startup watchdog for the descendant-cancellation test; detects a worker that never starts. |
| `internal/sandbox/native_test.go:106` | Keep 1m non-timeout fixture budget in the failed-run discard test; the timeout branch separately uses 100ms. Adapt fixture plumbing to the shared resolver. |
| `internal/sandbox/native_test.go:212` | Keep 1m outer bound for the opt-in real Codex boundary test; prevents a hung integration fixture. |
| `internal/sandbox/native_test.go:312` | Keep 2m outer bound for the opt-in authenticated Codex host-canary test; independent of agent policy defaults. |
| `internal/agent/review_test.go:274` | Keep 1m snapshot fixture bound; this test exercises file/total-byte limits rather than agent execution time. |

This revision addresses both required findings in the prior review, corrects native/input citations, records the accepted interactive semantics, and adds explicit reviewer-output coverage. Implementation remains subject to the independent plan gate. Planning only changes active artifacts. The snapshot has no Git metadata (`git status` reports “not a git repository”); Git-dependent verification belongs in implementation fixtures/a real checkout.

# ISSUE-57 verification plan

These are implementation-phase checks; planning does not claim they have passed. Use fake clocks and subprocess/fake-runtime fixtures, without model calls or a new OCI image. Add table-driven tests to existing package suites or focused `timeout_test.go`/`timeout_patch_test.go` files.

| Acceptance criterion | Concrete verification | Commands |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Config keys and invalid values | Contract tables cover omitted defaults, Go duration syntax, explicit empty, zero, negative, malformed and overflowing values, unknown roles, and invalid unselected overrides. Harness config decode and CLI fixtures require field-qualified failures from doctor and repo validate before execution. Repo validate uses a full trusted fixture base commit. | `go test ./internal/contract ./internal/harness ./internal/cli ./internal/validation` |
| 2. Defaults, idle exclusion, wall cap, shared resolver | Resolver tables cover all four roles, global values, role precedence, unattended 60m, native/delegated interactive cumulative active budget and 4h wall cap, OCI interactive 4h default and configured shorter limits. Fake clock advances through multiple turns: idle adds no active time, work accumulates, resuming never resets budget, wall timeout still fires during idle. Cover Codex, Claude, OpenCode, and OMP coordinator input boundaries; OMP pending tools/session settlement still count. Assert backend parity and positive operator overrides cannot extend policy. Assert resolver results explicitly clamp configured interactive active budgets (native/delegated) and wall limits (OCI) above 4h to 4h, while preserving the independent native/delegated 4h wall cap; unattended configured values remain unclamped. Cover shorter explicit global and role values, defaults, and role precedence on each backend. Validation remains min(15m, check.timeout): a 20m required check still receives a 15m effective deadline on host, native and OCI paths; assert no agent warning or recovery patch for validation. Delegated `ServeTools` remains usable past 15 simulated minutes under longer policy and exits on coordinator deadline/cancellation; verify transport and descendant cleanup without a real 15m wait. | `go test ./internal/contract ./internal/agent ./internal/sandbox ./internal/validation` |
| 3. Warning | Fake-clock boundary tests check min(2m, 10%), role/remaining-time text, one warning across pause/resume and competing wall/active thresholds, no warning after completion, and concurrent deadline/cancellation cleanup. Capture interactive stderr while blocked on input and headless progress output. | `go test -race ./internal/sandbox ./internal/agent` |
| 4. Recovery and unchanged worktree | Native/delegated execution and fake OCI fixtures modify/add/delete files then expire. Verify correct fixed relative patch path and configured and effective limits survive safe error masking; `errors.Is` retains DeadlineExceeded. Apply a complete text patch only in a disposable scratch fixture to verify its content. Compare checkout files, index, HEAD, existing PLAN/TEST_PLAN/REVIEW and lease artifact/checkpoint state before/after: only local recovery output may differ. Cover read-only output mapping, timeout during input, cumulative active timeout, and wall timeout. Cancellation/non-timeout failure must not masquerade as policy timeout. Reviewer timeout leaves live REVIEW.md unchanged, never imports partial role outputs, and RunReview never collects reviewer-timeout.patch as an artifact. | `go test ./internal/sandbox ./internal/agent ./internal/workflow ./internal/workspace` |
| 5. Doctor displays roles | CLI output fixture asserts planner/reviewer/developer/tester values, stable order, configured override, defaults, and interactive accounting/cap in text and existing JSON output. Invalid config produces nonzero exit with the offending field. | `go test ./internal/cli ./internal/harness` |
| 6. Required security/default regressions and make check | Commit trusted fixture config, change candidate timeout to a larger value, and verify the runner still expires at the trusted value; candidate invalid config also cannot replace approved authority. Exercise planner/reviewer/developer/tester construction. Reject symlink ancestors/destinations, linked source files, traversal, absolute paths, hardlinks, FIFO/device/socket entries without blocking or reading outside the sandbox. Enforce the decided 8 MiB total recovery bound; omit whole binary/oversized entries with coordinator notices and retain complete valid hunks for included entries. Bound file count, diff size, and recovery time; no partial unsafe artifact, and failure preserves the timeout cause. Test poisoned existing output, write failure, repeated recovery replacement, once-only warnings under race detector, OCI freeze/export/removal ordering, export failure cleanup, and all descendants stopped before native capture. Ensure timeout patch never imports, becomes a role artifact, enters a later snapshot, checkpoint, or submission, including pre-staged/tracked patches. | `go test -race ./internal/contract ./internal/agent ./internal/sandbox ./internal/workflow ./internal/workspace ./internal/pr ./internal/cli ./internal/validation`; `make check` |
| 7. Documentation | Review actual config tags against all examples; verify docs/project.md, recovery section in docs/developer.md, relevant harness limit guides and CHANGELOG.md are updated. Check relative links/anchors and parse changed bash blocks with `bash -n`; compare documented commands with Cobra registrations/help. Explain OCI wall-only accounting and manual patch recovery; preserve tool and validation deadlines. | `go run ./cmd/swarm repo doctor --help`; `go run ./cmd/swarm repo validate --help`; `git diff --check` plus link/snippet checks |

## Dedicated review regression cases

These cases are required in addition to the acceptance matrix; use injected time and real request/response fixtures so a long-lived context alone cannot satisfy the assertions.

| Case | Fixture and assertions | Commands |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1 — delegated tool-server lifetime (finding 1; AC2) | In `internal/sandbox/mcp_test.go` and delegated lifecycle tests, launch the coordinator-owned server under a longer resolved budget, use the shared injected clock to advance to 16m under a coordinator-resolved 60m budget and complete a real `swarm_*` request/response successfully. Exercise the actual delegated launch/hidden CLI wiring as well as ServeTools; ensure the fixture advances every timer source used by the server so the old independent 15m timer makes this test fail. A context-deadline assertion or merely advancing the budget clock while leaving a real server timer untouched is insufficient. Test deadline expiry and explicit cancellation separately; both close transports, stop in-flight tools and descendants, and leave no server running. Audit hidden CLI wiring in `internal/cli/internal_tools.go`; no agent-supplied duration may extend the coordinator lifetime. | `go test -race ./internal/sandbox ./internal/cli` |
| R2 — unchanged validation ceiling (finding 2; AC2/AC6) | Add a table-driven `TestValidationTimeoutCeiling` in `internal/validation/validator_test.go` or a focused new test file, with host, native and OCI subtests. Configure a required check at `20m` and exercise actual validation dispatch through each execution boundary after the agent caps are removed. Capture the effective context deadline: each path still gets `15m` (allow only elapsed setup time), or an earlier parent deadline in a separate case; OCI also receives an explicit `15m` check timeout. Keep `internal/validation/validator.go:133-139` and its 15-minute ceiling unchanged. Use injected time and execution fixtures to expire each check without a real 15-minute wait, asserting validation never picks up the agent budget, warnings or patch recovery; a shorter agent budget must not shorten validation either. Assert no warning is emitted, no recovery writer is invoked and no timeout patch is created. Retain shorter-check timeout coverage. The test must detect replacing the ceiling with the agent default or forwarding agent timeout behavior into validation. | `go test ./internal/validation ./internal/sandbox` |
| R3 — reviewer timeout output (note 6; AC4/AC6) | In agent review/isolation tests, seed live `.swarm/active/REVIEW.md`, `.swarm/active-output/REVIEW.md`, and authoritative artifact state, produce partial reviewer output in the sandbox, then expire the run. Exercise both adapter `OutputDir` handling (`isolated.go:44`) and the extra request-worktree snapshot in `RunReview`. Assert both live REVIEW.md files and registered artifacts remain byte-for-byte unchanged. The only new diagnostic output is `.swarm/active-output/reviewer-timeout.patch` in the intended live recovery directory, surviving temporary snapshot cleanup. Seed that patch for a subsequent RunReview and assert it is never read as REVIEW.md, returned or registered as a review artifact, or included in trusted gate inputs; only a successful fresh REVIEW.md can be imported. Cover recovery write failure without importing partial outputs. | `go test ./internal/agent ./internal/workflow` |

Implementation completion sequence:

```bash
make fmt
go build ./...
go test ./...
go vet ./...
make check
git diff --check
```

Run `make install` with a writable temporary `GOBIN` for the required hands-on CLI build, then inspect its `repo doctor --help` and `repo validate --help`. A real local OCI runtime smoke test is supplemental when available; required lifecycle coverage must run without a qualification image. Record skipped environmental checks and actual command outcomes in validation artifacts. Do not run coordinator claim/publication commands from the agent.

Before sign-off, run `grep -Rn 'time.Minute' internal --include='*.go'` and compare every occurrence with the PLAN inventory, including each individually listed test-only bound. Classify any added minute-based deadline as kept (with reason) or replaced; no grouped or unclassified entries. In particular, no independent 15m MCP lifetime may remain, while the validation 15m ceiling and 2m per-tool/snapshot/credential bounds remain intact.

Planning verification: inspected the existing source and all seven acceptance mappings; no implementation tests were run. This snapshot lacks Git metadata, so run Git-dependent fixture and final diff checks in an implementation checkout.

VERDICT: APPROVED

# ISSUE-57 plan review

Reviewed `.swarm/active/PLAN.md` and `.swarm/active/TEST_PLAN.md` against `.swarm/active/WORKUNIT.md` and the compiled `SYSTEM_PROMPT.md`. Spot-checked every "What we know" citation and the deadline inventory against the workspace source.

## Audit

| Item | Status | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Objective: configurable limits, higher defaults, idle exclusion, warning, patch preservation | Covered | Steps 2–7 cover all five parts. |
| C: Honor goals / rules, no protected paths | Covered | Step 8 explicitly leaves `.swarm/config.yaml`, schemas, prompts, workflows, validation and CI alone. `allow_harness_changes: false` is respected. |
| C: Timeouts load from approved base only; flags only shorten | Covered | Policy is held on the configured adapter, built from `LoadConfigAt(base)` (verified at `engine.go:247,434` and `claim_helpers.go:38`). Workers never reload config. The TEST_PLAN AC6 candidate-config regression is included. No new flags are added, and any operator override can only reduce the limit. |
| C: Timed-out run never mutates worktree, checkpoint or artifacts; patch written via `safefs`, never applied, checkpointed or submitted | Covered | Step 5 writes through `safefs.Root.Sub`/`WriteFile` (both exist at `internal/safefs/root.go:92,210`). Step 6 adds checkpoint and submission guards (`worktree.go:375` `git add -A`, `pr/service.go:764`, `worktree.go:163`), and the plan notes that an ignore rule alone is not enough. R3 covers reviewer output. |
| C: Validation check timeouts unchanged | Covered | `validator.go:133-139` stays as is. R2 shows the 15m ceiling holding on host, native and OCI once agent caps are removed from `withNativeWorkspace`/`RunWorker`. Removing those caps matters because `RunConfiguredNativeValidation` currently inherits the 15m cap from `withNativeWorkspace`, and the plan handles this correctly. |
| C: No new OCI turn protocol or qualification image | Covered | OCI interactive runs use wall-clock time only. Lifecycle tests use fake-runtime fixtures, and step 1 has an explicit stop-for-revision gate if pause/export cannot be done with existing primitives. |
| AC1 config keys and invalid values in doctor and validate | Covered | Validation sits in `ResolveExecution`, which is already called by `decodeConfig` (`scaffold.go:585`), doctor (`doctor.go:32`) and the validator (`validator.go:116`). |
| AC2 defaults, idle exclusion, 4h cap, OCI wall-only, one shared resolver | Covered | Semantics are decided and consistent. All four input waits are cited correctly (`native.go:287`, `delegated.go:171`, `opencode.go:131`, `omp.go:217`). |
| AC3 warning min(2m, 10%), once, shown in terminal | Covered | Includes a race-enabled once-only test and stderr capture while input is blocked. |
| AC4 bounded diff at `.swarm/active-output/<role>-timeout.patch`, path and limit in error, worktree untouched | Covered | 8 MiB bound. The typed error gets through the `runFailure` masking (`failure.go`) and keeps `errors.Is`. |
| AC5 doctor per-role resolved timeout | Covered | Step 7 plus TEST_PLAN row 5. |
| AC6 test coverage and `make check` | Covered | Every listed case maps to a row or to R1–R3. `make check` (= `lint race`) is in the completion sequence. |
| AC7 docs and CHANGELOG | Covered | `docs/project.md`, `docs/developer.md` (the "Recovering from an Interrupted Run" section exists at line 221), all five `docs/harness/` guides, and `CHANGELOG.md`. |
| Shape fit (Involved) | Adequate | Alternatives are given (a single context and per-turn reset are rejected with reasons), plus a probe step (step 1) and open questions with resolution steps. |
| Evidence | Verified | The `time.Minute` inventory matches exactly: 9 production lines across 8 sites, and 7 test lines. All cited symbols and files exist. |

## Findings (non-blocking)

1. The `internal/harness/scaffold.go:563` citation points to the start of `decodeConfig`. The `ResolveExecution` call itself is at line 585. The claim is accurate, but the line reference is imprecise.
2. Doctor reports the local repository config, not the approved base. That fits AC5, but the doctor output and the docs should say so, so operators don't treat it as the timeout that will actually be enforced.
3. The step 1 per-file and entry recovery limits are still open. Write the chosen values into the implementation notes and docs (AC7) so the patch bound is documented completely.
4. The MCP change (removing `mcp.go:16`) relies on coordinator cancellation reaching the hidden tool process. R1 has to fail against the current code, as the TEST_PLAN already says. Keep that requirement in place during implementation.
